newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Low offers seen in India's July diesel tender.
newsitem.headline: Low offers seen in India's July diesel tender.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp's (IOC) gas oil (diesel) import tender for July delivery attracted lower offers than the previous two tenders for May and June which traders said reflected the current soft market.

In its last tender for June, IOC awarded the 1.0-percent sulphur gas oil at more than $27 per tonne premium to the high of Mediterranean quotes, cost-and-freight (c-and-f) Indian east coast and more than $23 per tonne premium to Mediterranean quotes, c-and-f Kandla on the west coast.

But in this tender, offers related to the high of Mediterranean spot quotes for the 1.0-percent sulphur grade was more than $21 per tonne premium, c-and-f east coast, and more than $14 per tonne premium to the west coast.

But offers on a free-on-board basis were unchanged from the last tender, with Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) offering 1.0-percent sulphur gas oil at a 30-cent-per-barrel premium to MidEast spot quotes, and the 0.5-percent grade at a 45-cent premium to MidEast quotes.
Traders said KPC normally hold their fob offers steady at those levels and cut the costs through their more competitive freight rates.

Traders also noted that the fob offers were more than current levels in the MidEast which were assessed at close to parity to spot quotes for the 1.0-percent sulphur grade and between parity and a 10-cent premium for the 0.5-percent grade.
India was expected to take between 400,000 and 600,000 tonnes of gas oil in this tender, which are expected to be awarded later on Thursday, traders said.
They said this would not help boost the current soft market despite its higher volumes compared with the June tender when IOC took 315,000 tonnes of 1.0 and 0.25 percent sulphur gas oil.
